The present petition has been filed by the petitioners for grant of anticipatory bail in case having FIR No.185 dated 12.07.2022 registered under Sections 420, 120-B IPC at Police Station Division No.6, Ludhiana.

The FIR in this case was registered on the basis of the complaint lodged by Arshpreet Kaur wherein she stated that she got married with deceased Ranjit Singh who owned one residential house in the area of Miller Ganj, Ludhiana and one bank account and one car.
That petitioner No.1 is sister, while petitioner No.2 is nephew (Bhanja) of deceased-Ranjit Singh.
That Ranjit Singh died on 26.08.2021 due to some illness.

However, petitioner No.1 has forged one Will purported to be executed by Ranjit Singh in her favour and on the basis of the said forged Will, petitioner No.1 had withdrawn amount of Rs.17 lacs from the bank account of the deceased and petitioner No.2 took away the car

The counsel for the petitioner inter alia contends that the dispute with regard to validity of the Will in question is pending in Civil Court, Ludhiana.

That further petitioner No.1 has deposited an amount of Rs.12 lacs in the Court of Illaqa Magistrate concerned and has also joined the investigation with the Police in compliance of the previous order of interim bail passed by this Court.
Counsel for the petitioners has produced a copy of order dated 21.09.2022, passed by the Court concemed, whereby the petitioners have deposited the amount of Rs.12 lacs in the Court below.

sentences.text: The said order is ordered to be taken on record.
Learned State counsel, on instructions from HC Beant Singh, submits that there are allegations against petitioner No.1 that she fabricated one Will of her brother-Ranjit Singh who died on 26.08.2021.
He has not disputed the fact that the civil dispute between the parties with regard to illegality of the said Will is pending in the Court of Civil Judge, Ludhiana.
The State counsel has also not disputed the fact that the petitioners have joined the investigation and are not required by the Police for any further investigation or custodial interrogation.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and considered the submissions made by them.

The complainant has challenged one Will alleged to be executed by her husband Ranjit Singh in favour of his sister and his daughter regarding his entire property, on the ground that Ranjit Singh died intestate.
Admittedly, the dispute with regard to validity of the said Will, is pending in the Court of Civil Judge, Ludhiana on civil side.

Further petitioner No.1 has deposited amount of Rs.12 lacs in the Court | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this order/judgment of Illaqa Magistrate concerned and has also joined the investigation with the Police in compliance of the order dated 07.09.2022 passed by this Court.
Furthermore, the petitioners are not required by the Police for nay further investigation in the present case.
In view of the above, without commenting on the merits of the case, the present petition is hereby allowed and order dated 07.09.2022 is hereby made absolute.
The petitioners should abide by the conditions envisaged under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C.
The aforesaid deposit of Rs.12 lacs will be subject to final decision of the criminal case by the learned trial Court.
